questions.question: The relationship between variable input and output, keeping all other inputs constant is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**law of variable proportions**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Law of variable proportions** explains the relationship between variable input and output, keeping all other inputs constant.
 
• This law is crucial in the short-run production analysis where one input is variable while others are fixed.
 
• It highlights how output changes when the quantity of one input is varied, holding other inputs constant.
 
• The law is divided into three stages: increasing returns, diminishing returns, and negative returns.
 
• Understanding this law helps businesses optimize resource allocation and maximize production efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **total product** of a variable input is the total output produced by varying the quantity of the input.
 
• **Marginal product** refers to the additional output produced by using an extra unit of the variable input.
 
• The **law of diminishing marginal product** states that as more units of a variable input are added, the additional output (marginal product) eventually declines.
 
• These concepts are fundamental in microeconomics and help in understanding production functions and cost structures.

questions.question: Meenu alone can do a work in 16 days. Simi alone can do it in 12 days. If Raj joins them, they three together can complete the work in 4 days. How long will Raj alone take to finish the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Meenu alone can do the work in 16 days.

Simi alone can do the work in 12 days.

They three together can complete the work in 4 days.

**Formula used:**

Work rate of Meenu = (1)/(16) work/day

Work rate of Simi = (1)/(12) work/day

Work rate of Raj = (1)/(R) work/day

Combined work rate = (1)/(4) work/day

**Calculations:**

Combined work rate = Work rate of Meenu + Work rate of Simi + Work rate of Raj

(1)/(4) = (1)/(16) + (1)/(12) + (1)/(R) 

⇒ (1)/(R) = (1)/(4) - (1)/(16) - (1)/(12) 

⇒ (1)/(R) = (1)/(4) - (1)/(16) - (1)/(12) 

⇒ (1)/(R) = (12 - 3 - 4)/(48) 

⇒ (1)/(R) = (5)/(48) 

⇒ R = (48)/(5) days

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: If a person covers a distance of 90 km at a speed of 45 km/h and another distance of 150 km at a speed of 50 km/h, then his average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance₁ = 90 km

Speed₁ = 45 km/h

Distance₂ = 150 km

Speed₂ = 50 km/h

**Formula used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

**Calculations:**

Time₁ = Distance₁ / Speed₁

⇒ Time₁ = 90 / 45

⇒ Time₁ = 2 hours

Time₂ = Distance₂ / Speed₂

⇒ Time₂ = 150 / 50

⇒ Time₂ = 3 hours

Total Distance = Distance₁ + Distance₂

⇒ Total Distance = 90 + 150

⇒ Total Distance = 240 km

Total Time = Time₁ + Time₂

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 3

⇒ Total Time = 5 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 240 / 5

⇒ Average Speed = 48 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is**** 48 km/h**.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties were added in Constitution of India by which of the following amendments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the **42nd Amendment Act** in 1976.
 
• This amendment added a new part, Part IVA, to the Constitution, which consists of a single article, Article 51A.
 
• Article 51A lists ten fundamental duties for Indian citizens, which include respecting the Constitution, the national flag, and the national anthem, and promoting harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties aimed to remind citizens that while they enjoy rights, they also have duties to perform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **42nd Amendment** is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging changes to the Constitution.
 
• This amendment also brought about significant changes in the Preamble, the Seventh Schedule, and various other parts of the Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law, but they serve as a constant reminder to citizens of their responsibilities.
 
• Originally, there were ten fundamental duties; an eleventh duty was added by the 86th Amendment Act in 2002, which obligates parents to provide education to their children between the ages of 6 and 14 years.

questions.question:
In which of the following situations will the potential difference induced in the coil be the maximum?

(a) A bar magnet moving with a speed of 2 m/s towards a stationary coil

(b) A coil moving with a speed of 2 m/s towards a stationary bar magnet

(c) A coil and a bar magnet moving in the same direction with the speed of 2 m/s.

(d) A coil and a bar magnet moving towards each other with the speed of 2 m/s.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(d)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The maximum potential difference is induced in the coil when the relative speed between the coil and the bar magnet is the highest.
 
• In option (d), both the coil and the bar magnet are moving towards each other with a speed of 2 m/s each, resulting in a relative speed of 4 m/s.
 
• In options (a) and (b), the relative speed is 2 m/s as only one of the objects (coil or magnet) is moving.
 
• In option (c), both the coil and the bar magnet are moving in the same direction with the same speed of 2 m/s, resulting in a relative speed of 0 m/s.
 
• Therefore, the potential difference induced in the coil is maximum in option (d).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction, the induced electromotive force (EMF) in any closed circuit is equal to the negative of the time rate of change of the magnetic flux through the circuit.
 
• The relative motion between the coil and the magnet changes the magnetic flux through the coil, inducing a potential difference.
 
• Higher relative speeds result in a greater rate of change of magnetic flux and hence a higher induced potential difference.

questions.question:
Two coils, A and B, such that A is connected to a battery through a key and B is connected to a galvanometer, are arranged parallel and close to each other. During which of the following duration will the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction be observed?

(a) Two minutes after closing the key.

(b) During the interval the key is taken out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (b)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electromagnetic induction** is observed when there is a **change in the magnetic flux** linked with a coil.
 
• In the given scenario, electromagnetic induction will not occur two minutes after closing the key because the system would have reached a steady state by then.
 
• However, during the interval when the key is taken out, there is a change in the current through coil A, which changes the magnetic flux linked with coil B, thus inducing a current in coil B.

questions.question: If the roots of quadratic equation (2 − p)x² + 2px − (p + 1) = 0 are equal, then the value of p is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The quadratic equation is (2 − p)x² + 2px − (p + 1) = 0.

The condition for equal roots in a quadratic equation is that the discriminant (D) must be zero.

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant D is given by:

D = b² − 4ac

**Formula used:**

Discriminant (D) = b² − 4ac = 0 for equal roots

**Calculation:**

For the given equation (2 − p)x² + 2px − (p + 1) = 0:

Here, a = (2 − p), b = 2p, and c = −(p + 1).

Step 1: Apply the discriminant formula:

D = b² − 4ac

Substitute the values of a, b, and c:

D = (2p)² − 4(2 − p)(−(p + 1))

Step 2: Simplify:

D = 4p² − 4(2 − p)(−(p + 1))

D = 4p² − 4[(2 − p)(−p − 1)]

Step 3: Expand the terms inside the brackets:

(2 − p)(−p − 1) = −2p − 2 + p² + p

= p² − p − 2

Step 4: Substitute back into the equation:

D = 4p² − 4(p² − p − 2)

D = 4p² − 4p² + 4p + 8

D = 4p + 8

Step 5: Set the discriminant to 0 for equal roots:

4p + 8 = 0

⇒ 4p = −8

⇒ p = −2

**∴ The value of p is −2.**

• Each carbon atom in benzene forms three σ-bonds: two with adjacent carbon atoms and one with a hydrogen atom.
 
• The three π-bonds are formed by the overlapping of p-orbitals above and below the plane of the carbon atoms.
 
• In total, benzene has **15 bonds** (12 σ-bonds + 3 π-bonds).
 
• The resonance stabilization of benzene makes it more stable compared to other unsaturated hydrocarbons.

• Benzene is a fundamental component in organic chemistry and is widely used in the production of various chemicals and polymers.
 
• Due to its aromatic nature, benzene undergoes substitution reactions rather than addition reactions, preserving its stable ring structure.
 
• Exposure to benzene is hazardous and can cause serious health effects, including leukemia and other blood disorders.
